## Saturday, August 15

Fifteen games, and **six City Connects on one slate.** San Francisco in the Gigantes black, the Mets in the concrete gray NYC set, Tampa Bay, Cincinnati in the red, Atlanta in the light blue, and the Dodgers in the cream. That is the most this log has carried in a single day, and it is not a coincidence. Saturday is the City Connect slot for several clubs by standing rule, the Mets and Dodgers among them, so the alternates cluster the way they do on Friday nights.

**Only five of the fifteen home teams wore white**, the Tigers, Cubs, Guardians, Astros and Angels. Everyone else reached for something, and the road teams stayed conventional to balance it: seven road grays against eight visiting alternates.

Powder blue had its best day of the season with three separate entries. St. Louis wore it in Chicago, Kansas City wore it in Anaheim, and Toronto wore its own at home against the Yankees. Two of those were on the road, which is where the colour belongs and where almost nobody uses it any more.

Sacramento's gold was the other standout, worn against a Texas road gray. It is the loudest home jersey in the league right now and the only one built around a city the team is only passing through, which makes it the strangest good-looking uniform in baseball.

<div style="margin: 2em 0 0.6em; padding: 0.7em 1.1em; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #C41E3A 0%, #A5C8E1 100%); border-radius: 12px 12px 0 0;">
  <span style="font-size: 0.72em; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #f5f5f5;">&#9918; Jersey of the Day</span>
  <span style="display: block; font-size: 1.15em; font-weight: 900; color: #ffffff; margin-top: 3px;">Cardinals Powder Blue</span>
</div>

<blockquote class="twitter-tweet" data-dnt="true"><a href="https://twitter.com/Cardinals/status/2088764714532614201"></a></blockquote>

Powder blue is a road colour, and almost nobody treats it like one any more. Most of the teams that own a light blue alternate save it for a Sunday at home, where it competes with a white uniform it was never designed to sit next to. St. Louis wore this one at Wrigley Field, against Chicago in home whites, which is exactly the frame it was built for.

The birds on the bat are the reason it works. That mark is busy by any modern standard, two cardinals, a yellow bat, a lot of small shapes, and on a white or gray jersey it can turn muddy at distance. Powder blue is light enough to keep the contrast and saturated enough that the red pops off it rather than sinking in. The chest is the whole uniform here and the background finally lets it breathe.

It also solves a problem the Cardinals have all season, which is that their two primary looks are nearly interchangeable on television. Home white and road gray with the same chest mark and the same red cap is a wardrobe with one idea in it. The powder blue is the only jersey St. Louis owns that changes the picture, and they should be reaching for it far more than they do.

<div style="margin: 2em 0 0.6em; padding: 0.7em 1.1em; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #4a4a4a 0%, #1a1a1a 100%); border-radius: 12px;">
  <span style="font-size: 0.72em; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #d0d0d0;">&#128078; Stinker of the Day</span>
  <span style="display: block; font-size: 1.15em; font-weight: 900; color: #ffffff; margin-top: 3px;">Mets NYC City Connect</span>
</div>

<blockquote class="twitter-tweet" data-dnt="true"><a href="https://twitter.com/Mets/status/2088764453554667697"></a></blockquote>

This is the most thought-through City Connect in the league on paper and one of the least effective on a field, and both of those things are true at once.

The research is genuinely good. The base is concrete gray for the city, the pinstripes are built from the circles and diamonds of the MTA's local and express symbols, the purple runs through the details for the 7 line that carries people to Citi Field, and there is a subway token on the sleeve. Read the design brief and it is hard to argue with any single decision.

Then you watch a game in it. Concrete gray reads as dirty white on broadcast, the purple is a thin accent that disappears past about ten rows, and the subway pinstripes resolve into ordinary pinstripes at any real distance. What is left is a gray jersey with black letters on it, worn by a team whose actual identity is one of the loudest orange-and-blue combinations in sport. Almost nothing that makes this concept interesting survives the trip to a television screen.

The lettering is the other problem, and it is a choice rather than an execution issue. **NYC** claims the entire city on a uniform worn by the Queens team, in a market where the other club already owns the New York shorthand. The Mets have a borough, a colour scheme and a script nobody else can use. Dressing them in municipal gray trades all of that for a concept you have to be told about.

## Friday, August 14

Fourteen games on the board, all fourteen logged, and it was the loudest colour night of the month. **Nine of the ten home teams skipped white.** Cincinnati in the black City Connect, Pittsburgh in theirs, Detroit in orange, the Mets in black, Cleveland in the navy City Connect, Tampa Bay in the Devil Rays throwback, Atlanta in red, Toronto in the navy City Connect, and Houston in orange. Only the Cubs broke the pattern, and they broke it upward, going to the light blue rather than the home whites.

That is a full inversion of Wednesday, when all fifteen home clubs wore white and every alternate in baseball belonged to a visitor. Tonight the visitors did the opposite: six of the ten came in gray, and only Boston in red, San Diego in the sand pinstripes, Chicago in black, and Seattle in navy brought anything else.

The Friday effect is doing most of this work. The Mets wear black at home every Friday, City Connects cluster on Friday nights across the league, and the result is a slate where the colour is concentrated rather than scattered. Kansas City opened the west coast window in the road gray against an Angels home white — the first time the plain Angels home white has appeared in this log, as against the 1980s throwback they usually reach for. The west coast then delivered the two best-looking games of the night: the Athletics in kelly green against a Rangers road gray, and Colorado's purple against San Francisco's orange, which is the rarest colour-on-colour pairing the schedule can produce.


<div style="margin: 2em 0 0.6em; padding: 0.7em 1.1em; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #003831 0%, #EFB21E 100%); border-radius: 12px 12px 0 0;">
  <span style="font-size: 0.72em; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #f5f5f5;">&#9918; Jersey of the Day</span>
  <span style="display: block; font-size: 1.15em; font-weight: 900; color: #ffffff; margin-top: 3px;">Athletics Green Alternate</span>
</div>

<blockquote class="twitter-tweet" data-dnt="true"><a href="https://twitter.com/Athletics/status/2088486789694829013"></a></blockquote>


Kelly green and gold is the most underused colour pair in American sport, and this is the only team that owns it. Nobody else in baseball is within reach of this green. It is not forest, it is not hunter, it is not the safe dark green a brand consultant reaches for when they want green without commitment. It is loud, and it has been loud since the early seventies.

The jersey earns the day because it does almost nothing beyond letting the colour work. Gold script, gold piping down the placket, white pants underneath so the green reads at full strength instead of getting muddied by a matching bottom. There is no gradient, no secondary logo crowding the chest, no attempt to modernise a look that was already right.

It is also worth saying plainly, given where this franchise is: a team in a temporary ballpark with an unresolved future still puts the best colour combination in the league on the field most nights. The uniform is the most stable thing about the Athletics right now.

<div style="margin: 2em 0 0.6em; padding: 0.7em 1.1em; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #4a4a4a 0%, #1a1a1a 100%); border-radius: 12px;">
  <span style="font-size: 0.72em; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #d0d0d0;">&#128078; Stinker of the Day</span>
  <span style="display: block; font-size: 1.15em; font-weight: 900; color: #ffffff; margin-top: 3px;">Blue Jays Navy City Connect</span>
</div>

<blockquote class="twitter-tweet" data-dnt="true"><a href="https://twitter.com/BlueJays/status/2088464692477878321"></a></blockquote>


Toronto is one of the easiest cities in baseball to dress. The club owns a royal blue nobody confuses for anyone else, a maple leaf with more instant recognition than most franchise marks, and a colour scheme already tied to a national identity. The City Connect throws all of it away and comes back with navy.

Navy is what a team picks when it cannot decide. It is the safest colour in sport, it is already worn by a third of the league, and on this jersey it actively fights the one element that should carry the design. The red accents want a bright field to sit against, the way red sits on white on the Canadian flag. Against navy they go dull, and the whole thing reads closer to a generic road alternate than a tribute to a specific place.

The frustrating part is that the concept had somewhere obvious to go. Red and white is right there, unclaimed, nationally understood, and used by nobody else in the league. Toronto had the clearest brief of any City Connect and answered it with the colour that says the least.

  <p style="font-size: 1.05em; font-weight: 900; margin: 0; text-align: center; color: #9bc824;">Matchup Grade: 8.5 / 10</p>

Purple against orange is the loudest frame the schedule can produce, and it almost never happens, because both of these are alternates that have to be chosen on the same night by two clubs with no reason to coordinate. Colorado's purple is a true violet rather than a navy pretending, and San Francisco's orange is the actual orange from the cap, not a muted jersey version of it.

What makes it work rather than clash is the value match. Both tops sit at nearly the same darkness, so neither one flattens the other on camera, and both teams paired them with gray or white below rather than doubling down. The result is two saturated blocks of colour at the same weight, which reads as a deliberate pairing even though nobody planned it.

The one thing keeping it off a 9 is the caps. Colorado's black crown drains a little energy out of the purple, and a purple cap on purple would have pushed this into the best-looking game of the month.

## Thursday, August 13

Nine games on the board and the road teams brought the colour again. All nine are final, and five of the first six visitors skipped the gray or wore it as the whole look: Cleveland in navy at Detroit, Cincinnati in the red script at Rate Field, Pittsburgh in the black alternate rather than the City Connect for the second straight night, Seattle in navy at Yankee Stadium after leading with the Northwest Green there on Wednesday, and Boston and Chicago in road grays at Toronto and Washington.

The split that stands out is at home. Five of the six home clubs wore white, and Washington was the only one to answer with colour, pulling the navy alternate against the Cubs' gray. That is the inverse of Wednesday, when all fifteen home teams wore white and every alternate belonged to a road team.

The two late games are Milwaukee at the Dodgers, where the Brewers went to the powder blue against a Dodgers home white, and Texas at the Angels in a road gray against Anaheim's home white. Both finished late, Milwaukee taking a one-run game and the Angels shutting out Texas. The game that mattered most tonight: **Philadelphia at Minnesota at the Field of Dreams site in Dyersville, Iowa.** Both clubs have released special uniforms for it, and it takes both of our daily honours below.

<div style="margin: 2em 0 0.6em; padding: 0.7em 1.1em; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #C4CED4 0%, #E81828 100%); border-radius: 12px 12px 0 0;">
  <span style="font-size: 0.72em; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #f5f5f5;">&#9918; Jersey of the Day</span>
  <span style="display: block; font-size: 1.15em; font-weight: 900; color: #ffffff; margin-top: 3px;">Phillies Field of Dreams Gray</span>
</div>

<blockquote class="twitter-tweet" data-dnt="true"><a href="https://twitter.com/Phillies/status/2088015648903274619"></a></blockquote>


Philadelphia went with gray rather than cream, and that is the call that makes this set. Everybody expects a Field of Dreams uniform to be cream, because cream is the shorthand for old, and the Twins went there. The Phillies went the other way and it reads more like a jersey that actually existed than a costume of one.

The script is the reason. Red "Phillies" with a black outline and that long tail sweeping under the word is the best wordmark the franchise owns, and on a plain gray field with red and black piping running the placket, there is nothing competing with it. No nameplate clutter, no gradient, no drop shadow. The whole jersey is one shape.

The detail to look for on the broadcast is the **1839 Baseball Centennial patch on the right sleeve**, which both clubs are wearing tonight. It is the small piece that ties the game to the reason it exists, and it is doing more work than any amount of manufactured vintage would.

Two takes on the same brief, and they split cleanly. Minnesota did the expected thing beautifully: cream with navy pinstripes, the red "Twins" script outlined in navy with a tail running under it, the most literal reading of 1930s baseball you can build. Philadelphia refused the cream entirely and put its best script on plain gray.

Side by side, the gray is what keeps this from being two cream jerseys blurring into the corn. Cream against gray gives you an actual value difference on camera, which matters at a ballpark with no stands behind the outfield and nothing but green and sky in the background. Both sleeves carry the 1839 Baseball Centennial patch.

## Wednesday, August 12

Fifteen games again, the same fifteen pairings as Tuesday, and the wardrobe went the other way. Nine alternates on Tuesday became ten on Wednesday, and for the second straight night not a single City Connect came out of a closet. What changed is where the colour sat: every one of the ten alternates belonged to the road team. Ten visiting clubs skipped the gray, and all fifteen home teams wore white or cream.

That is a genuinely unusual split. The road gray is the most-worn uniform in baseball and it appeared only five times all night, on the Cubs, Red Sox, Mets, Reds and Phillies. Everybody else who travelled brought colour: Cleveland and Minnesota and Tampa Bay and Milwaukee in navy, Pittsburgh in the black alternate rather than the City Connect, Colorado in purple, Houston in orange, Kansas City in powder blue, Texas in the royal, and Seattle in the Northwest Green at Yankee Stadium. San Francisco supplied the only cream. Our Matchup of the Day is in Toronto, where two of the most classic looks in the sport met with no colour at all.

<div style="margin: 2em 0 0.6em; padding: 0.7em 1.1em; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #007878 0%, #f5f5f5 100%); border-radius: 12px 12px 0 0;">
  <span style="font-size: 0.72em; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #f5f5f5;">&#9918; Jersey of the Day</span>
  <span style="display: block; font-size: 1.15em; font-weight: 900; color: #ffffff; margin-top: 3px;">Mariners Northwest Green Alternate</span>
</div>

<blockquote class="twitter-tweet" data-dnt="true"><a href="https://twitter.com/Mariners/status/2087723769184043402"></a></blockquote>

The Northwest Green is the best colour any team currently runs and it does not get out often, so a road wearing at Yankee Stadium is a gift. Against the pinstripes it looked even better than it does at home, because the Yankee white is the most neutral backdrop in the sport and it let the teal carry the entire frame. The 50th-season patch on the sleeve is the detail worth noticing this year, a small anniversary mark that sits on the shoulder without fighting the arched MARINERS script. Seattle has three good looks and this is the one to lead with.

## Tuesday, August 11

Fifteen games, thirty uniforms, and a slate that split almost exactly down the middle between the plain and the interesting. Twenty of the thirty were classics, ten road grays against ten home whites, which is the baseline the schedule keeps returning to. What lifted the night was where the colour landed: nine alternates and the first City Connect the league has worn since the weekend.

The alternates clustered in the West and the AL. Seattle brought the navy into Yankee Stadium, Minnesota answered Baltimore's gray with its own navy, Colorado went purple in Arizona against the Sedona red, and Tampa Bay's navy ran into the Athletics in the light green. Milwaukee and Kansas City both travelled in powder blue on the same night, which is the best accident on the board, and Miami pulled out the black alternate rather than the City Connect. San Francisco supplied the only City Connect of the evening, the black set, against a Houston road gray. Our Matchup of the Day is in Sacramento, where the Rays' navy met the Athletics' green.

<div style="margin: 2em 0 0.6em; padding: 0.7em 1.1em; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #005A9C 0%, #f5f5f5 100%); border-radius: 12px 12px 0 0;">
  <span style="font-size: 0.72em; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #f5f5f5;">&#9918; Jersey of the Day</span>
  <span style="display: block; font-size: 1.15em; font-weight: 900; color: #ffffff; margin-top: 3px;">Dodgers Home White</span>
</div>

<blockquote class="twitter-tweet" data-dnt="true"><a href="https://twitter.com/Dodgers/status/2087383206761050255"></a></blockquote>

There is no trick to it, which is exactly why it wins. The Dodger home white is the least complicated great uniform in baseball: script across the chest, red number under it, blue cap, and nothing else asking for attention. On a night when nine clubs reached for an alternate to make an ordinary Tuesday feel like an event, Los Angeles put on the same thing it has worn for seventy years and still had the best-looking frame on the board. Kansas City's powder blue across from it did not hurt either, one soft colour against a clean white being about as easy on the eye as the sport gets.

## Monday, August 10

Ten games on a Monday, and the wardrobe stayed quiet the way Mondays usually do. Sixteen of the twenty uniforms were classics, plain home whites and road grays, and there was not a single City Connect anywhere in the league, which is exactly what the calendar predicts now that those have settled into Friday and Saturday slots. Every road team except one wore the gray.

The colour that did show up came in four places. Baltimore brought the orange alternate to Minneapolis, Arizona went to the black alternate at home against Colorado, Tampa Bay wore the navy in Oakland, and Milwaukee kept rolling in the powder blue, which is their road set rather than an alternate and still the best-looking travel uniform in baseball. Our Matchup of the Day is in St. Louis, where Philadelphia's road gray met the Cardinals' home white. No colour at all, just two of the most storied classic uniforms in the National League sharing a field, and sometimes that is the whole point.

<div style="margin: 2em 0 0.6em; padding: 0.7em 1.1em; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #12284B 0%, #9ecae1 100%); border-radius: 12px 12px 0 0;">
  <span style="font-size: 0.72em; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #f5f5f5;">&#9918; Jersey of the Day</span>
  <span style="display: block; font-size: 1.15em; font-weight: 900; color: #ffffff; margin-top: 3px;">Brewers Powder Blue</span>
</div>

<blockquote class="twitter-tweet" data-dnt="true"><a href="https://twitter.com/Brewers/status/2087000586361122984"></a></blockquote>

The powder blue is technically Milwaukee's road uniform, not an alternate, and that is the whole reason it wins tonight. Most clubs treat the gray as a tax they pay for leaving home. The Brewers decided their travel look should be the prettiest thing they own, and the result is a jersey that makes every road broadcast better than it needed to be. Against San Diego's home white at Petco it read like a throwback to a decade when teams were not afraid of a soft colour.

## Sunday, August 9

All fifteen of Sunday's games are logged below, and Sunday is the day the calendar jerseys come out. Both of the league's standing Sunday traditions turned up: the Mariners in the cream Steelheads throwback at T-Mobile and the Padres in the camouflage at Petco, two clubs that have quietly built a weekly ritual most of the sport has not bothered to copy. Add the Giants in the cream at Oracle and the Phillies in the cream at Citizens Bank and that is four uniforms on the board that only exist because of what day it is. Not one City Connect appeared anywhere in the league, two days after eleven of them turned up on a single Friday night.

The colour moved to the road. Seven visiting clubs skipped the gray: the Angels in red for a fourth straight game in Miami, the Orioles in orange at Texas, the Astros in orange at San Diego, the Dodgers in the blue in Phoenix, and three separate navies from the Guardians, Tigers and Rays. The other eight road teams all wore the gray.

At home the count ran seven classics against eight alternates. The Marlins broke out the teal throwback, the Royals and Rangers both went powder blue on the same afternoon, Washington wore the red, and Pittsburgh went back to the black alternate a day after it was our Jersey of the Day. The best pairing of the afternoon was in Arlington, where Baltimore's orange ran into Texas in the powder blue. It was the only game on the board with no white and no gray anywhere in the frame, one warm colour against one cool one, and it is our Matchup of the Day.

<div style="margin: 2em 0 0.6em; padding: 0.7em 1.1em; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #0A0A0A 0%, #3BA39C 100%); border-radius: 12px 12px 0 0;">
  <span style="font-size: 0.72em; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #f5f5f5;">&#9918; Jersey of the Day</span>
  <span style="display: block; font-size: 1.15em; font-weight: 900; color: #ffffff; margin-top: 3px;">Marlins Teal Throwback</span>
</div>

<blockquote class="twitter-tweet" data-dnt="true"><a href="https://twitter.com/Marlins/status/2086574839951700151"></a></blockquote>

This is our No. 1 Marlins jersey and the only A in their closet, and Sunday is the only day you can see it. Miami hands the 1993 teal a standing Sunday home slot, which means the best thing the franchise owns is also the hardest to catch. The formula is simple enough that it is strange nobody copies it: one loud colour that belongs to exactly one team, a block wordmark with the swoosh underline, a legacy patch on the sleeve, and white pants so nothing competes with the teal. The Retro Wave spends an entire concept trying to say that Miami is bright and a little bit 1990s. The teal just is.

## Saturday, August 8

All fifteen games are in, and Saturday was the mirror image of Friday. A night after eleven clubs wore a City Connect, exactly one did: the Nationals in the District Blueprint. Nine home teams went to the plain white or the pinstripes. The six that reached for something else all had a reason: the Cardinals in the cream, which carries the "St. Louis" script and is reserved for Saturday home games at Busch, the Royals in the powder blue, the Giants in the Gigantes, the Pirates in the black alternate, the Diamondbacks in the black, and Washington in the City Connect. The road is where the rest of the colour went: the Braves and Twins in navy, the Rays in navy, the Orioles in black, the Rockies in purple, the Angels in red for a third straight night at Miami, and the Dodgers in the blue alternate in Phoenix. Nine of the fifteen visitors still wore the gray.

<div style="margin: 2em 0 0.6em; padding: 0.7em 1.1em; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #111111 0%, #FDB827 100%); border-radius: 12px 12px 0 0;">
  <span style="font-size: 0.72em; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #f5f5f5;">&#9918; Jersey of the Day</span>
  <span style="display: block; font-size: 1.15em; font-weight: 900; color: #ffffff; margin-top: 3px;">Pirates Black Alternate</span>
</div>

<blockquote class="twitter-tweet" data-dnt="true"><a href="https://twitter.com/Pirates/status/2086259452231995775"></a></blockquote>

The Pirates own the best black jersey in baseball and it is not particularly close. The reason is the gold. Most teams that go black treat it as a blank canvas and then trim it in something safe, which is how you end up with a jersey that reads as a placeholder. Pittsburgh runs the black against a real, saturated yellow-gold, and that single colour does all the work: the script pops, the piping reads from the upper deck, and the cap matches instead of approximating. It also helps that this is a genuine alternate rather than a novelty, so it looks like a uniform the team owns rather than a costume it borrowed for a night.

## Friday, August 7

All fifteen games are in, and Friday belonged to the City Connects. Seven clubs wore one at home: the Pirates in the black, the Red Sox in the Fenway green, the Marlins in the Retro Wave, the White Sox in the red, the Brewers in the Wisco, the Royals in the white, the Cardinals in The Lou, the Rangers in the Tejas, the Diamondbacks in the purple, the Padres in the navy, and the Mariners in the Rush-Blue. That is the heaviest City Connect night of the season so far, which is what Friday is built for. The visitors barely varied: thirteen of the fifteen road clubs wore the gray, with only the Angels in red at Miami and the Rays in navy at Seattle breaking it. At home the plain white showed up in just three parks, the Yankees and Phillies in the pinstripes and the Giants in the orange Friday alternate.

<div style="margin: 2em 0 0.6em; padding: 0.7em 1.1em; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #0C2C56 0%, #1f6fd0 100%); border-radius: 12px 12px 0 0;">
  <span style="font-size: 0.72em; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #f5f5f5;">&#9918; Jersey of the Day</span>
  <span style="display: block; font-size: 1.15em; font-weight: 900; color: #ffffff; margin-top: 3px;">Mariners City Connect</span>
</div>

<blockquote class="twitter-tweet" data-dnt="true"><a href="https://twitter.com/Mariners/status/2085943743983796729"></a></blockquote>

The Rush-Blue is the rare City Connect that reads as a real uniform rather than a costume, and it is the best-looking thing anyone put on Friday. The blue is genuinely its own colour, not a borrowed royal, and pairing it with the black pants gives the whole silhouette a weight that most City Connects never find because they stop at the shirt. Seattle also resisted the two traps that sink this category: there is no novelty wordmark shouting a nickname, and there is no gradient. It is a strong colour, clean lettering, and a matching cap, which is all a good uniform has ever needed.

## Thursday, August 6

All eleven games are in, and the road teams ran the day completely. Eight of the eleven visitors turned up in colour: red for the Angels in Baltimore, blue for the Mets in Cleveland, black for the Pirates in Milwaukee, black for the Marlins in Atlanta, black for the White Sox in Boston, royal for the Blue Jays at Wrigley, navy for the Tigers in Seattle, navy for the Twins in Kansas City, and brown for the Padres in Phoenix. Only the Athletics and the Nationals wore the gray. At home it was white in nine parks, with Milwaukee in the cream and Philadelphia in the powder blue.

<div style="margin: 2em 0 0.6em; padding: 0.7em 1.1em; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #A6CAEC 0%, #284898 100%); border-radius: 12px 12px 0 0;">
  <span style="font-size: 0.72em; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #f5f5f5;">&#9918; Jersey of the Day</span>
  <span style="display: block; font-size: 1.15em; font-weight: 900; color: #ffffff; margin-top: 3px;">Phillies Powder Blue</span>
</div>

<blockquote class="twitter-tweet" data-dnt="true"><a href="https://twitter.com/Phillies/status/2085537565097030042"></a></blockquote>

Thursday at Citizens Bank Park means powder blue, and it is the most reliable standing uniform slot in baseball. Nothing else in the league is this locked to a day of the week, which is why "what do the Phillies wear on Thursday" is a question people actually type. The uniform earns the attention: a soft, almost pastel blue with the maroon-and-white script across the chest, the powder blue cap, and a silhouette lifted straight out of the late 1970s. Most throwback-adjacent looks feel like a costume for one night. This one has been worn often enough to just be part of who the Phillies are.

Detroit's navy against Seattle's home white was the cleanest separation on the slate. The Tigers' navy is a genuinely dark navy rather than a washed-out one, so it reads as a solid block against the Mariners' whites instead of turning muddy under the lights, and the orange "Detroit" script is the only warm colour on the field. Simple, high-contrast, and it did not need a City Connect to be the best-looking game of the night.

## Wednesday, August 5

All fifteen games are in, and the road teams ran the day. Seven of the fifteen visitors turned up in colour: royal for the Blue Jays in Houston, navy for the Rays in Denver and the Twins in Kansas City, red for the Angels in Baltimore, black for both the Marlins in Atlanta and the Pirates in Milwaukee, and brown for the Padres in Phoenix. The other eight wore gray. At home it was the usual near-sweep of white, twelve of fifteen, broken by Cleveland in the red alternate, Milwaukee in the cream, and Arizona closing the night in Sedona red.

<div style="margin: 2em 0 0.6em; padding: 0.7em 1.1em; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #BD3039 0%, #0C2340 100%); border-radius: 12px 12px 0 0;">
  <span style="font-size: 0.72em; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #f5f5f5;">⚾ Jersey of the Day</span>
  <span style="display: block; font-size: 1.15em; font-weight: 900; color: #ffffff; margin-top: 3px;">Red Sox Home White</span>
</div>

<blockquote class="twitter-tweet" data-dnt="true"><a href="https://twitter.com/RedSox/status/2085191606483698004"></a></blockquote>

Seven road teams wore colour on Wednesday and Boston still took the day in the plainest thing on the schedule. The Fenway home white is a hundred years of restraint in one shirt: the hanging-sox wordmark in red, the thin red soutache tracing the placket and the sleeves, navy cap, and nothing else asking for attention. It is the uniform every "classic" argument eventually points at, and the reason is that there is nothing in it to date. Strip the modern fabric and this reads the same in 1935 as it does tonight. On a slate with brown, cream and two different reds competing for the eye, the whites were the best-looking thing on television.

Fifteen games, and this is the only one where neither team wore white. San Diego brought the brown with the gold script, Arizona answered in Sedona red, and the result is the rarest thing on a baseball schedule: a broadcast with no neutral half. Brown and red should not work together, two warm colours close enough on the wheel to muddy each other, and the reason it does is the gold. It sits on the Padres' chest and sleeves and gives the eye somewhere cool to land between the two heavy tones. Put this on any night of the season and it stands out. On a Wednesday where eight visitors wore gray, it is not close.

## Tuesday, August 4

A full fifteen-game slate, and for once the road teams refused to blend in. Nine visitors went with gray, but the other six brought colour: the Angels in red, the White Sox and Pirates both in black, the Rays in navy, the Padres in brown, and the Dodgers in royal blue. Every single home team wore white or cream, which is the cleanest split we have logged all season.

<div style="margin: 2em 0 0.6em; padding: 0.7em 1.1em; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #005A9C 0%, #1c1c1c 100%); border-radius: 12px 12px 0 0;">
  <span style="font-size: 0.72em; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #f5f5f5;">⚾ Jersey of the Day</span>
  <span style="display: block; font-size: 1.15em; font-weight: 900; color: #ffffff; margin-top: 3px;">Dodgers Blue Alternate</span>
</div>

<blockquote class="twitter-tweet" data-dnt="true"><a href="https://twitter.com/Dodgers/status/2084822046928949254"></a></blockquote>

The royal blue alternate is the one Dodgers look that does not rely on the script doing all the work. On the whites and the grays that arced "Dodgers" is the entire uniform; on the blue it has to share the frame with the colour, and it holds up. The red number keeps its warmth against the darker base, and the whole thing reads cleanly under lights in a way most coloured alternates do not. Fifteen games on the schedule and this was the one worth stopping on.

The only game all year where both teams are called the Sox, and they could not have looked more opposite. Chicago in the black alternate with the silver diagonal script, Boston in the home whites with the red script and the navy outline. Black against white, silver against red, the plainest possible palette on both sides and not a single wasted mark between them. Two clubs that figured out their look decades ago and have spent every year since refusing to touch it.

## Monday, August 3

A quiet eight-game Monday to open the week, and the road teams may as well have carpooled: seven of the eight visitors wore gray, with only Tampa Bay breaking rank in the light blue. The colour came almost entirely from the home dugouts. Houston pulled out the white "Stros" City Connect it saves for Monday home games, Colorado wore the purple, Milwaukee went cream, and San Diego travelled in the sand pinstripes. The Dodgers' road grays take Jersey of the Day, Cardinals at Yankees is our Matchup of the Day, and the slate grades out to about 6.8.

<blockquote class="twitter-tweet" data-dnt="true"><a href="https://twitter.com/Dodgers/status/2084430324440900094"></a></blockquote>

The cursive "Dodgers" script in blue on gray with the red number underneath is one of the least complicated uniforms in baseball and one of the hardest to improve on. There is no wordmark trick, no gradient, no concept to explain, just a script the club has barely touched in decades sitting on a plain gray base. At Wrigley, against a Cubs side in its own white pinstripes, it made for the most classically dressed frame of a quiet Monday. Jersey of the Day.

Two of the most decorated franchises in the sport sharing a field, and neither reached for anything: St. Louis in the road grays with the birds-on-bat, New York in the home pinstripes. No alternates, no City Connects, nothing invented this decade. On a night when seven of eight road teams wore gray, this is the pairing where that plainness reads as pedigree rather than absence, and it takes Matchup of the Day on the strength of the two uniforms alone.

## Sunday, August 2

A full 15-game Sunday, and Sunday is the one day of the week with standing uniform traditions built into it. San Diego pulled out the camouflage military jersey it wears every Sunday home game, Seattle wore the black-and-cream Steelheads throwback that now owns Steelheads Sundays at T-Mobile Park, and the Mets went back to the Cooperstown pinstripes for a second straight day. Add Baltimore's orange, Houston's navy, the Royals in royal blue against Colorado's purple, and the Angels in the Surf City cream, and there was plenty of colour underneath a board that leaned heavily on grays. The Mets throwback repeats as Jersey of the Day, Red Sox at Dodgers takes Matchup of the Day, and the slate grades out to about 7.2.

<div style="margin: 2em 0 0.6em; padding: 0.7em 1.1em; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #002D72 0%, #FF5910 100%); border-radius: 12px 12px 0 0;">
  <span style="font-size: 0.72em; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #f5f5f5;">⚾ Jersey of the Day</span>
  <span style="display: block; font-size: 1.15em; font-weight: 900; color: #ffffff; margin-top: 3px;">Mets Cooperstown Throwback</span>
</div>

<blockquote class="twitter-tweet" data-dnt="true"><a href="https://twitter.com/Mets/status/2083935203198722248"></a></blockquote>

Back-to-back for the Cooperstown pinstripes, and we are not going to pretend otherwise: this is still the best jersey anyone put on this weekend. The racing-stripe piping over both shoulders and down the V-neck is the detail that carries it, a 1980s cue almost nobody in baseball wears anymore, and the blue script with the orange outline sits perfectly on the pinstriped white. Forty years on from the 1986 title, the uniform holds up better than most of what the league is putting out new. Jersey of the Day again.

Boston's road grays against the Dodgers' home whites is the classic version of this sport, and the second straight night these two shared a field in Chavez Ravine. No alternates, no throwbacks, no City Connects, just the red script on gray against the cursive Dodgers script on white, two of the most recognisable uniforms in baseball with nothing dressed up. It does not have the colour of a Tigers-Athletics frame, but on pedigree and cleanliness it is the best-looking broadcast of the day. Matchup of the Day.

## Saturday, August 1

A full 15-game Saturday, and the two best looks on the board were both history lessons. The Mets broke out the Cooperstown pinstripes with the shoulder piping to mark 40 years since their last World Series, and it is the sharpest thing anyone wore all night. Cincinnati debuted the new red City Connect, Tampa Bay went charcoal in theirs, and Detroit's navy script against the A's Sacramento gold gave us the loudest colour clash of the day. Jersey of the Day goes to the Mets throwback, the Tigers and Athletics take Matchup of the Day, and the slate grades out to about 7.5.

<div style="margin: 2em 0 0.6em; padding: 0.7em 1.1em; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #002D72 0%, #FF5910 100%); border-radius: 12px 12px 0 0;">
  <span style="font-size: 0.72em; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #f5f5f5;">⚾ Jersey of the Day</span>
  <span style="display: block; font-size: 1.15em; font-weight: 900; color: #ffffff; margin-top: 3px;">Mets Cooperstown Throwback</span>
</div>

<blockquote class="twitter-tweet" data-dnt="true"><a href="https://twitter.com/Mets/status/2083656409053343971"></a></blockquote>

The Mets pulled out the Cooperstown Collection pinstripes to mark 40 years since the 1986 title, and it is a beauty: white pinstripes, the racing-stripe piping running over both shoulders and down the V-neck, and the blue script with the orange outline. That shoulder piping is the detail that makes it, a genuinely 1980s design cue almost nobody wears anymore. Easy Jersey of the Day.

## Friday, July 31

A full 15-game Friday, and the City Connects came out in force: the Reds and Orioles in black, the Blue Jays and Padres in navy, the Rockies in purple, the Angels in the Surf City cream, and the Mariners in blue. Add the Rays' white Devil Rays throwback, Arizona's Sedona red, and Houston's orange, and this was one of the most colourful slates of the season. The Mets' black alternate takes Jersey of the Day, Rangers royal blue at Astros orange is our Matchup of the Day, and the slate grades out to about 7.5.

<div style="margin: 2em 0 0.6em; padding: 0.7em 1.1em; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #002D72 0%, #1c1c1c 100%); border-radius: 12px 12px 0 0;">
  <span style="font-size: 0.72em; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #f5f5f5;">⚾ Jersey of the Day</span>
  <span style="display: block; font-size: 1.15em; font-weight: 900; color: #ffffff; margin-top: 3px;">Mets Black Alternate</span>
</div>

<blockquote class="twitter-tweet" data-dnt="true"><a href="https://twitter.com/Mets/status/2083285208086827028"></a></blockquote>

New York's black alternate is the rare black jersey that earns it: the orange-and-blue script pops off the dark base instead of getting swallowed by it, and the whole thing reads sharp rather than moody. On a night stacked with City Connects trying hard to be different, the Mets won by wearing the best-balanced jersey on the board. Jersey of the Day.

## Thursday, July 30

A 10-game Thursday heavy on the home whites, with the color coming from the alternates: the Rangers and Royals in royal blue, the Cubs in blue, the Pirates and Marlins in black, the Nationals and Mariners in navy, and the Mets in the blue alternate for the sharpest frame of the night against Miami's black. The Dodgers' home whites take Jersey of the Day, the Marlins-Mets black-on-blue is our Matchup of the Day, and the slate grades out to about 7.0.

## Wednesday, July 29

A full 16-game Wednesday, headlined by a Braves-Mets split doubleheader at Citi Field, the makeup of Tuesday's rainout. The color stayed steady across the slate: the Reds broke out the red, the Diamondbacks the Sedona red, the Royals went powder blue, the Mariners their navy, the Angels the cream Surf City City Connect, and the Mets closed the nightcap in the black alternate. The Mets take Jersey of the Day, the Red Sox-Athletics classic gray-on-white crossover is our Matchup of the Day, and the slate grades out to about 6.9 out of 10.

## Tuesday, July 28

Fifteen games on the board Tuesday, headlined by a Guardians-Reds split doubleheader in Cincinnati, and the color skewed toward the alternates once the sun went down. Cleveland went road gray in the day game and broke out the navy Diamond C at night, Arizona brought the Sedona red, Toronto and Milwaukee both reached for powder blue, and the Athletics ran their kelly green out on a Tuesday. San Francisco wore the black SF Fog City Connect and the Angels countered Houston with the cream Surf City City Connect. The A's green takes Jersey of the Day, the Mariners-Dodgers navy-on-white marquee is our Matchup of the Day, and the slate grades out to about 7 out of 10. Atlanta's game at the Mets was postponed.

The A's don't usually pull the kelly green on a Tuesday, it's their Green Friday staple, but they broke it out early this week and it's still the brightest thing in the closet. Gold “Athletics” script glowing on that bright kelly base, straight from the Charlie Finley heyday, and it's an easy Jersey of the Day.

## Monday, July 27

A full 11-game Monday to open the week, and the color came out early. The Braves and Mariners both reached for navy, the Blue Jays and Brewers went powder blue, the Diamondbacks wore black, and Detroit debuted the Motor City City Connect in front of the home crowd. The Mets' classic home whites take Jersey of the Day, the storied Yankees-White Sox crossover is our Matchup of the Day, and the slate grades out to about 6.9 out of 10.

## Sunday, July 26

Fifteen getaway-day games, and Sunday dialed the color back a notch from Saturday, a lot of home whites and road grays, but a few clubs kept the party going. The Orioles broke out the orange, the Marlins wore their throwback teal against San Diego's brown, and the Rays ran the Devil Rays look back. The Orioles' orange alternate is our Jersey of the Day, the Angels-Giants classic-on-classic frame is our Matchup of the Day, and the slate grades out to about 7 out of 10.

## Saturday, July 25

Fifteen more games the day after Hall of Fame Weekend, and the alternates and City Connects kept right on coming. The Rays broke out the beloved Devil Rays throwback, the Reds and Cardinals turned in a red-vs-powder-blue color clash, San Diego brought the brown, and the Dodgers and Mets — stuck in plain primaries Friday for a [movie shoot at Citi Field](/stories/mets-dodgers-standard-uniforms-emma-stone-movie) — finally cut loose in their blue and black alternates. The Rays' Devil Rays set takes Jersey of the Day, that Dodgers-Mets alternate clash is our Matchup of the Day, and the slate grades out to about 7 out of 10.

<div style="margin: 2em 0 0.6em; padding: 0.7em 1.1em; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #1c1c1c 0%, #6cc24a 55%, #8FBCE6 100%); border-radius: 12px 12px 0 0;">

  <span style="display: block; font-size: 1.15em; font-weight: 900; color: #ffffff; margin-top: 3px;">Rays Devil Rays Throwback Alternate</span>
</div>

<blockquote class="twitter-tweet" data-dnt="true"><a href="https://twitter.com/RaysBaseball/status/2081178015556313429"></a></blockquote>

Nobody had more fun on Saturday than Tampa Bay. The Devil Rays throwback — a white jersey with the rainbow-gradient “Devil Rays” wordmark arched across the chest — is a full trip back to the franchise's late-'90s origins, and it was easily the best-dressed look of the night. The Rays even won in it, and “Saturday Night Fever” fit the vibe perfectly.

## Friday, July 24

Fifteen games and one of the most fun uniform nights of the season, because this was [Hall of Fame Weekend](/stories/mlb-throwback-caps-hall-of-fame-weekend-2026). All 30 clubs wore throwback caps to mark the induction ceremony, and the jerseys followed suit with a City Connect and alternate blowout: the Rays' Devil Rays fauxback, Boston's green CC, the Rangers' red Tejas set, Baltimore's cream-and-green BMORE, Philadelphia's blue Philly, and plenty more. Only one game on the entire slate had both teams in their standard uniforms, and there is a reason for that, which we get into below. The Angels' throwback “Los Angeles” caps take Jersey of the Day, the clean Dodgers-Mets primary matchup is our Matchup of the Day, and the slate grades out to 8 out of 10.

<div style="margin: 2em 0 0.6em; padding: 0.7em 1.1em; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #BA0021 0%, #1c1c1c 100%); border-radius: 12px 12px 0 0;">
  <span style="font-size: 0.72em; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #f5f5f5;">⚾ Jersey of the Day</span>
  <span style="display: block; font-size: 1.15em; font-weight: 900; color: #ffffff; margin-top: 3px;">Angels Throwback “Los Angeles” Caps</span>
</div>

<blockquote class="twitter-tweet" data-dnt="true"><a href="https://twitter.com/Angels/status/2080808306034274741"></a></blockquote>

On a night when all 30 teams wore throwback caps for Hall of Fame Weekend, the Angels' was our favorite. Los Angeles paired the road gray with a vintage “Los Angeles” cap, a clean nod to the franchise's California Angels era, and it was the sharpest of the throwback lids across the league. It is a simple change, just a cap, but it turned a plain road-gray look into the best-dressed detail of the day.

## Thursday, July 23

A five-game Thursday getaway slate, and it played about as quiet as that number suggests. Four of the five home teams reached for a white or a classic, the road clubs did most of the talking in their alternates, and nothing on the board came close to the color a full Friday delivers. Atlanta's home white was the sharpest thing in a dull room and takes Jersey of the Day, the Rays and Blue Jays get Matchup of the Day almost by default, and San Diego's brown ran for a seventh straight game. The slate grades out to 6.5 out of 10.

On a night this short on color, the cleanest classic wins by default, and Atlanta's home white is a very good classic. The lowercase Braves script across the chest, the tomahawk underline, and the navy-and-red trim on a crisp white is one of the more timeless looks in the National League, and it does not need a gimmick to carry a broadcast. It is not the flashiest jersey on any given night, but on a quiet Thursday it was the sharpest thing on the field.

The quiet end of a quiet night. Kansas City went with the road gray and the basics, no powder blue in sight, and Detroit stayed in the home whites with the Old English D. Gray against white is the plainest frame the sport offers and there was nothing here to change that, but the Tigers' clean home look kept it from bottoming out.

## Wednesday, July 22

Seventeen games, the biggest slate this tracker has logged in a single day, and we have Tuesday's rain to thank for it. Both games washed out at Yankee Stadium and Fenway came back as doubleheaders, and both twin bills ran the identical wardrobe script: road gray in the afternoon, black alternate under the lights. Twelve alternates hit the field in all and not one City Connect, which is exactly what a Wednesday is supposed to look like. The color that did show up was worth the wait, with the Rays and Blue Jays running their third blue-on-blue in four days for our Matchup of the Day, Kansas City finally reaching for the powder blue, Detroit's navy earning Jersey of the Day, and San Diego's brown hitting a sixth straight game. The slate grades out to 7.3 out of 10.

<blockquote class="twitter-tweet" data-dnt="true"><a href="https://twitter.com/Tigers/status/2080125012674056230"></a></blockquote>

Detroit's navy alternate is the quiet success story of the 2026 uniform year. The orange Detroit script sitting on navy gives the Tigers something their gray road set never has, which is warmth, and it manages to look brand new while borrowing nothing but the team's own colors. It travels well too. Against Wrigley Field's pinstripes it read cleanly all afternoon, and Hao-Yu Lee's three-run homer in it was the highlight of Detroit's day. This is how you add an alternate without wandering away from who you are.

Three blue-on-blue games in four days between these two, and this is the best-looking one yet because they finally swapped ends of the spectrum. Tuesday it was Tampa Bay in the light blue against Toronto in the royal. Wednesday the Rays went to the deep navy with the sunburst RAYS wordmark and the Blue Jays answered in the powder blue, so instead of two mid-tone blues competing for the same space you get the darkest jersey either club owns against the lightest. That is how you do a single-color matchup: pick opposite ends and let the contrast carry it. No white and no gray anywhere in the frame for the second straight meeting, and the Rogers Centre roof kept the light even enough that both blues read true on camera.

The orange Detroit script on navy is warmer and more legible than anything the block-D grays give you, and against Wrigley's white pinstripes with the red C it makes a proper old-school National League frame out of an interleague game. Miami's road gray is the most improved gray in baseball since the rebrand, with the black-outlined Miami script and the blue and red trim giving it more life than most, and Houston's home whites with the navy ASTROS wordmark and the orange piping are as clean as that franchise has looked in a decade. ## Tuesday, July 21

Rain took two games off the board, with the Pirates at Yankees and the Orioles at Red Sox both postponed, and the 13 that survived split hard between the clubs that dressed up and the clubs that clocked in. Eight teams went out in plain road gray and eight in home whites, but the color that did show up was excellent: the Rays and Blue Jays ran blue on blue for our Matchup of the Day, the Twins and Guardians both reached for alternates, San Diego's brown hit a fifth straight day, and the Dodgers went back to the royal blue. The slate grades out to 7.4 out of 10.

<div style="margin: 2em 0 0.6em; padding: 0.7em 1.1em; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #005A9C 0%, #1c1c1c 100%); border-radius: 12px 12px 0 0;">

  <span style="display: block; font-size: 1.15em; font-weight: 900; color: #ffffff; margin-top: 3px;">Dodgers Royal Blue Alternate</span>
</div>

<blockquote class="twitter-tweet" data-dnt="true"><a href="https://twitter.com/Dodgers/status/2079759189518225542"></a></blockquote>

The Dodgers have been leaning on the royal blue alternate more and more, and it is the correct instinct. The blue with the white Los Angeles script across the chest is a better jersey than either gray they own, it photographs cleanly under the lights, and it gives a team that spends most of its road schedule in muted gray an actual identity on the field. Max Muncy put a two-run homer into the night in it at Citizens Bank Park. More of this, please.

Nothing else on this board put two colors on the field with no white and no gray anywhere in the frame.

## Monday, July 20

Monday nights are usually when the wardrobe goes quiet, and this 15-game slate mostly proved it: nine teams in plain road gray, eight in home whites or pinstripes, and exactly one City Connect on the entire board. The clubs that did put color on the field carried the night. The White Sox and Rangers gave us black against the cleanest whites in baseball for our Matchup of the Day, the Rays and Blue Jays went blue on blue, the Mets' royal alternate met Milwaukee's home cream, Houston broke out the white "Stros" City Connect, and the Angels wore the white throwback alternate for a second straight day. The slate grades out to 7.3 out of 10.

<div style="margin: 2em 0 0.6em; padding: 0.7em 1.1em; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #BA0021 0%, #1c1c1c 100%); border-radius: 12px 12px 0 0;">

  <span style="display: block; font-size: 1.15em; font-weight: 900; color: #ffffff; margin-top: 3px;">Angels White Throwback Alternate</span>
</div>

<blockquote class="twitter-tweet" data-dnt="true"><a href="https://twitter.com/Angels/status/2079433697749819557"></a></blockquote>

Back-to-back Jersey of the Day honors for the same uniform, and it earned them again. The Angels' white throwback alternate, arched red "Angels" script, halo floating over the A, California patch on the sleeve, walked off the Cardinals on a hit by pitch and looked better doing it than anything else on the Monday board. This is the jersey the Angels should be wearing every home game.

The ColorWay Clash of the Day, and it is a study in how far clean beats busy. Chicago's black alternate with the gothic SOX wordmark is the sharpest thing in a wardrobe that has not had much to celebrate, and Texas answered with the whitest whites in the league, that unbroken cream-free home set with the royal and red piping running down the placket. Black against pure white is the oldest contrast in the book, and under the Globe Life roof it reads like a tuxedo. No City Connect, no throwback, no gimmick, just two teams wearing their best plain clothes.

The only City Connect on the entire Monday board, and it is one of the good ones. Houston wore the white Space City jersey, the navy ASTROS wordmark cut through by the big orange-to-yellow gradient star, the nebula-print sleeve trim, and the "we choose to go to the moon" line stitched down by the hem. Miami answered with the plain black alternate, script Marlins in teal and red, not the Retro Wave City Connect. Black against a white City Connect gives the Astros' star and sleeve gradients all the room they need, and it is the rare Monday game where somebody actually dressed up.

## Sunday, July 19

Sunday in baseball means throwback and alternate jerseys, and this 16-game slate delivered the goods: the Mariners debuted the black-and-cream Steelheads throwback in a walk-off win, the Tigers' brand-new navy alternate met the Angels' white throwback alternate in our Matchup of the Day, Paul Skenes pitched in the Pirates' black alternate right on schedule, and the White Sox and Blue Jays went full color-on-color. The Sunday slate grades out to 7.3 out of 10.

## Saturday, July 18

Saturday flipped the wardrobe from Friday's City Connect night to a loaded alternate jersey showcase: 15 games, a Cleveland doubleheader, and some of the best uniform pairings of the week. The Cardinals' Victory Blue jersey steals Jersey of the Day, the Braves' light blue City Connect and the Red Sox's yellow Boston marathon jersey kept the color coming, the Athletics broke out the gold "Sacramento" script, and a Mets-Phillies rivalry classic in road gray and cream takes the Matchup of the Day crown. The Saturday slate grades out to 7.2 out of 10.

## Saturday, July 11

A big 16-game Saturday, headlined by the Brewers and Pirates finally playing Friday's rained-out game as part of a doubleheader in Pittsburgh. Saturday brought the color the midweek slates lacked: City Connects for the Giants and Blue Jays, powder blue for the Brewers and Royals, the Cardinals' cream, the Astros' orange, and a stack of alternates. Slate average: 7.0 out of 10.

## Friday, July 10

Fourteen games, with Brewers at Pirates rained out and rescheduled as a Saturday doubleheader, a washout that also claimed the Pirates' Friday-home black City Connect. The rest of the league more than covered for it: eight City Connects hit the field in one night after two straight nights of zero, exactly the weekend pattern this tracker was built to prove. Only two home teams stayed in white, seven road teams stayed in gray, and 19 of the 28 uniforms on the field were alternates or City Connects. Slate average: 7.5 out of 10, the best-dressed night of the log so far.

## Thursday, July 9

The full 13-game slate is in the books. A mostly classic Thursday: a dozen home teams in white or cream, six road teams in the standard grays, and eight clubs reaching for an alternate. No City Connects. Slate average: 6.9 out of 10.

## The Pattern Engine: Running Uniform Counts

This is where the tracker earns its keep over time. Every look gets counted, and as the days stack up this section becomes the evidence file behind every "what jersey are they wearing today" question: how often each team wears each uniform, and which days of the week each alternate actually shows up. Twenty-four days in, we have logged 319 games and 638 individual uniforms. 55 different alternates and throwbacks account for 229 of them. Here is the alternate board.

Seattle's navy is the most-worn alternate in baseball right now at 13, just ahead of the Pirates' black at 12 and the Padres' brown at 10, and all three are really road uniforms in everything but name. That is the quiet story of the alternate board: the jerseys at the top are not special-occasion pieces, they are teams that have effectively replaced a gray with something with colour in it.

The day-of-week rhythm is still the clearest pattern in the data, and it has held up as the sample has grown. 27 different City Connects have been worn 48 times, and 32 of those 48 came on a Friday. Add the 9 Saturdays and Friday plus Saturday accounts for 85 percent of every City Connect we have logged. The seven that fall outside are three Mondays, two Tuesdays, one Wednesday and one Sunday, and midweek slates keep confirming the shape: plenty of alternates, almost no City Connects. Houston is the reason Monday keeps creeping up, because the white "Stros" kit is tied to Monday home games.

The one club that ignores the calendar entirely is the Angels. Their cream Surf City City Connect is the most-worn City Connect on the board at 5, and it has come out on a Tuesday, a Wednesday, a Friday, a Saturday and a Sunday. Nobody else has worn one on more than two different days of the week. If you are trying to predict an Angels home game, the City Connect is genuinely live any night, which is not true of the other 29 teams.

The other reliable rhythm is the Sunday matinee, where the powder blues, creams and throwbacks come out. Two of them are now formal standing traditions rather than tendencies: San Diego wears the camouflage jersey for every Sunday home game, and Seattle's new black-and-cream Steelheads throwback owns every Sunday home game at T-Mobile Park. Around them, the Blue Jays and Rangers powder blues, the Giants and Brewers creams, and the Marlins, Rays and Mets throwbacks have all used the Sunday slot.

Two exceptions still prove the Friday rule. The Pirates' Friday-home black City Connect missed one week only because the game itself was rained out, and the Nationals were the lone club to skip their slot by choice, wearing the navy alternate instead of the District Blueprint. Friday is officially City Connect night in 2026, and the log now has three weeks of receipts.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**What is the MLB daily uniform tracker?**

It is a running log of what every MLB team actually wore in every game, updated each morning after the previous night's slate. Every jersey and uniform gets recorded, from home whites and road grays to alternates, City Connects, and throwbacks, and every matchup gets a ColorWay grade for how the two looks paired on the field.

**What jersey is my team wearing tonight?**

Open your team's page from the uniform schedule grid above. It maps every fixed jersey day the club runs, like Friday City Connects, Sunday creams, or powder blue day games, so you can call tonight's look before first pitch. Then check back here tomorrow morning, because this tracker logs the uniform every MLB team actually wore, every single day.

**How do I find out what jersey the Dodgers or Yankees are wearing tonight?**

The [Dodgers uniform schedule](/stories/dodgers-uniform-schedule-2026) and [Yankees uniform schedule](/stories/yankees-uniform-schedule-2026) pages predict tonight's jersey from each team's day-of-week rotation, and the daily log on this page records what they actually wore last night, from home whites to City Connects. The same goes for all 30 clubs through the team pages above, so the question has an answer both before and after every game.

**How do you know what uniform each team wore?**

We check every game the morning after using game photos and broadcast footage from the night before, then log both teams' uniforms. When something is ambiguous, like a City Connect versus a similar regular alternate, we verify against multiple dated game photos before recording it.

**How often do MLB teams wear their City Connect uniforms?**

Most City Connect uniforms follow a fixed weekly slot. The Pirates wear their all-black 2026 City Connect for Friday home games, the Reds wear their pinstriped City Connect 2.0 on Saturdays, and most other clubs use similar weekend anchors. The running counts on this page will show the real frequency as the season plays out.

**Do MLB teams always wear white at home and gray on the road?**

No, and that is exactly why this tracker exists. White at home and gray on the road is the default, but on the Friday, July 10 slate alone, 19 of the 28 uniforms on the field were alternates or City Connects. Some clubs, like the Phillies, follow a strict published rotation, while others swap in alternates whenever the mood or the starting pitcher calls for it.

**When do MLB teams wear their alternate jerseys?**

It varies by team. Some alternates have fixed days, like Friday reds or Sunday creams, while others are manager's choice or a starting pitcher's preference. That day-of-week data is exactly what this tracker is built to surface, and the pattern section above fills in with evidence as the days accumulate.

## The Bottom Line on the MLB Daily Uniform Tracker

Baseball puts on more uniforms than any other sport, and nobody logs what actually hits the field each night. That is the gap this page fills: every team, every game, every day, graded and counted, with the day-of-week patterns emerging as the record grows. Bookmark it, check it with your morning coffee, and when you want to know what your team wears next, the [full uniform schedule guide](/stories/mlb-uniform-schedule-2026) has the forward-looking answer.
